promotionalText: Share live heart rate, workouts, and HRV with a coach. Train with zones and intervals, review your progress, and save workouts to Apple Health.
description:
Connect a Bluetooth heart-rate monitor to see live BPM at a glance, train with zones and intervals, measure HRV and recovery, and share a workout with your coach.

BPM keeps the important number big and the controls close at hand.

LIVE HEART RATE

• Connect compatible Bluetooth Low Energy heart-rate monitors
• See current, average, minimum, and maximum BPM, plus your current zone
• Set custom zones, threshold tones, and spoken zone alerts
• Follow heart rate and workout timing on your Lock Screen and Dynamic Island

WORKOUTS

• Run a simple timer or build reusable work/rest presets
• Track sets, recovery, heart-rate charts, and estimated calories
• Return directly to an active workout, including paused sessions
• Save workouts with a title and notes, or use optional AI voice to draft them for your review
• Sync saved workouts, heart-rate samples, and active calories to Apple Health
• Review and autofill calorie settings from Apple Health when you choose
• Keep workout history synced through iCloud

TRAIN TOGETHER

• Invite a coach, trainer, or friend with a link or temporary six-digit code
• Share live heart rate, workout timing, sets, and HRV measurements
• Let your training partner start, pause, and control the shared workout or load a preset
• Keep your own view of the workout while controls stay synchronized
• Stop sharing at any time; sessions also expire automatically

RECOVERY

• Measure two-minute HRV using RMSSD from a compatible monitor's RR intervals
• Track heart-rate recovery during cooldowns
• Review HRV and workout history over time

SAVE AND SHARE

• Create workout cards with charts, statistics, and your choice of accent color
• Choose the time range to include before sharing
• Export readable summaries or attach detailed JSON logs

BPM is built for chest straps and other BLE monitors. A compatible external heart-rate monitor is required for live measurement; HRV requires RR-interval support. Accuracy and available data depend on your sensor. Calorie values are estimates. BPM is not a medical device and is not intended to diagnose or treat any condition.

whatsNew:
• Share a live workout with a coach or friend using an invitation link. Keep timers, sets, and workout controls in sync across devices.
• Start and follow an HRV measurement together, with the result calculated on the monitor owner's device.
• Review and autofill calorie settings from Apple Health.
• Reopen BPM directly to your active or paused workout.
• Clearer HRV readiness and connection messages, improved Live Activities, and more reliable sharing and session recovery.
reviewNotes:
BPM 2.2 (24) adds live workout invitation links and synchronized trainer controls, shared HRV, optional Apple Health autofill, and session reliability improvements. No sign-in or purchase is required.

HARDWARE: Live measurement requires a physical Bluetooth Low Energy heart-rate monitor supporting the standard GATT Heart Rate Service (UUID 0x180D). Wear or activate the monitor, grant Bluetooth permission, open Device using the heart icon, and select it. Without a monitor, BPM displays ---; it does not measure heart rate with the phone camera. HRV requires RR intervals from a compatible monitor such as Polar H10. Remain still for the two-minute recording. Invalid or incomplete recordings are rejected.

LIVE SHARING: On the monitor owner's phone, open Device and start sharing. Send the invitation link or six-digit code to a second device running BPM. Open the link, or enter the code in Device and tap Connect. The viewer can follow heart rate, workout timers and sets, load a preset, and start/pause/control the workout. HRV initiated from either device runs on the monitor owner's device; the viewer mirrors its progress and result. Anyone with the code or link can view and control the shared session. Sharing stops after five minutes if nobody joins, or after 90 minutes total, and can be stopped manually. The owner's local workout continues after sharing stops.

HEALTH: In Settings, open the calorie setup and choose Apple Health autofill. Grant read access, review the available values and dates, then tap Autofill to fill compatible empty settings. Existing entries are preserved. BPM derives age from date of birth without storing the date of birth. Imported weight, age, sex, resting heart rate, and VO2 max remain on device and are excluded from iCloud preferences, live-sharing payloads, and AI voice requests. Estimated calories calculated from these settings can appear in a shared workout. Saving a workout can write workout, heart-rate, and calorie data to Apple Health with permission.

HISTORY AND CARDS: Save a workout, open Workout History, tap its row, then use Share. Chart and Stats cards support an editable title, time range, and accent color. Plain Text and Logs open the native share sheet; Logs attaches a JSON file. Save Image requests add-only photo-library permission.

AUDIO: Settings offers BPM threshold tones and spoken zone alerts. Workout Presets offer Play Sound for work/rest/cooldown and completion cues. A successful HRV measurement also plays a cue. The audio background mode supports these intermittent workout alerts; bluetooth-central supports monitor communication.

AI VOICE: In Save Workout, tap AI voice, grant microphone permission, record up to 60 seconds, and tap Send. The first-use Send recording? prompt names OpenAI and explains the recording, including spoken health details, is sent for transcription and workout notes. Allow & Send permits upload; Cancel keeps it local. Review and correct the result before saving. Manual entry works without AI. Reset AI voice permission in Settings to repeat consent. Recording stops when backgrounded. Measured heart rate, HealthKit records, and workout history are not attached to this request.

Privacy details: https://bpmtracker.app/privacy.html. BPM is not intended to diagnose or treat medical conditions.
